archivedDataNotice: Reference component masses, power budgets, data rates, and costs calibrated from NASA Ames State-of-the-Art of Small Spacecraft Technology, MODIS/VIIRS, LRO, and SCaN open publications.

sources.label: NASA Ames — State-of-the-Art of Small Spacecraft Technology
NASA EOS — MODIS & VIIRS Active Fire Instrument Reference
NASA LRO — Diviner, LEND & LAMP Lunar Polar Instruments

parts.name: Small MicroSat Bus (12U / ESPA-Class)
parts.hintText: Compact aluminum-honeycomb chassis ideal for rideshare and small rockets; saves mass and money but offers less thermal margin.
parts.sourceLabel: NASA Ames State-of-the-Art of Small Spacecraft Technology (Structures)

parts.name: Medium Spacecraft Bus (ESPA-Grande Class)
parts.hintText: Reinforced bus with extra radiation shielding and multi-instrument mounts, built for high-altitude GEO or deep-space lunar missions.
parts.sourceLabel: NASA Ames Small Spacecraft Technology — Platform Bus Standards

parts.name: Body-Mounted GaAs Solar Panels
parts.hintText: Zero moving parts and virtually impossible to jam after launch, but limited surface area caps available power at ~65 W.
parts.sourceLabel: NASA Ames SmallSat SOA — Power (Solar Cells)

parts.name: Deployable Twin-Wing Solar Array
parts.hintText: Unfolds in orbit to deliver 180 W—enough for high-rate X-band radios and multiple thermal cameras.
parts.sourceLabel: NASA Ames SmallSat SOA — Deployable Solar Arrays

parts.name: High-Efficiency Gimbaled ROSA Array
parts.hintText: Roll-Out Solar Array with dual-axis sun tracking. Maximizes wattage for Ka-band links and multi-sensor payloads.

parts.name: 40 Wh Li-Ion Battery Pack
parts.hintText: Light and inexpensive energy storage for low-power LEO satellites, but struggles during long GEO equinoxes or heavy camera night passes.
parts.sourceLabel: NASA Ames SmallSat SOA — Energy Storage

parts.name: 120 Wh Space-Grade Li-Ion Battery
parts.hintText: Triple the energy reserve so thermal cameras and radios keep working through Earth or Lunar shadow without browning out.
parts.sourceLabel: NASA Ames SmallSat SOA — Li-Ion Flight Heritage

parts.name: S-Band Patch Antenna (2.2 GHz)
parts.hintText: Low-power telemetry antenna (~12 GB/day). Works for simple sensors, but causes memory overflow if paired with high-resolution imagers.
parts.sourceLabel: NASA Near Space Network (SCaN) — S-Band Links

parts.name: X-Band High-Gain Dish (8.4 GHz)
parts.hintText: Standard Earth-observation downlink (~65 GB/day). Draws more power and requires accurate pointing, but clears camera memory during short passes.
parts.sourceLabel: NASA Near Space Network — X-Band Earth Observation

parts.name: Ka-Band Steerable Phased Array (26 GHz)
parts.hintText: Ultra-high-bandwidth downlink (150 GB/day) for multi-instrument payloads. Requires deployable solar wings or ROSA to feed its RF amplifier.

parts.name: Basic Flight Computer (32 GB Flash)
parts.hintText: Affordable C&DH processor with 32 GB buffer. If ground stations drop out or downlink lags behind, memory fills quickly.
parts.sourceLabel: NASA Ames SmallSat SOA — Command & Data Handling

parts.name: Radiation-Hardened OBC (128 GB SSR)
parts.hintText: Triple-modular redundant flight computer with 128 GB solid-state recorder; survives solar particle events and holds days of backlog during outages.
parts.sourceLabel: NASA Ames SmallSat SOA — Radiation-Tolerant Avionics

parts.name: 3-Axis Magnetorquers & Sun Sensors
parts.hintText: Lightweight magnetic coils that push against Earth's magnetic field. Low power, but lacks the precision pointing needed in GEO or Moon orbits.
parts.sourceLabel: NASA Ames SmallSat SOA — Guidance, Navigation & Control

parts.name: Reaction Wheels + Dual Star Trackers
parts.hintText: Precision pointing stability (<0.01°) for sharp thermal maps, high-gain X-band dishes, and lunar polar targeting where magnetic fields are absent.
parts.sourceLabel: NASA Ames SmallSat SOA — Precision ADCS

parts.name: Thermal Infrared Imager (VIIRS / MODIS Class)
parts.hintText: Detects active fire heat signatures day and night in 3.7–11 µm infrared bands (0.53 km ground pixel at 700 km SSO). Generates 24 GB/day.
parts.sourceLabel: NASA MODIS / VIIRS Thermal Anomalies & Fire Specs

parts.name: Visible / NIR Pushbroom Camera
parts.hintText: High-resolution daytime smoke & burn-scar camera (0.20 km at LEO, 0.35 km at SSO), but generates 32 GB/day—outstripping an S-band radio.
parts.sourceLabel: NASA MODIS — 250-500 m Visible/NIR Bands (reference imager)

parts.name: Wide-Field GEO Fire-Watch Telescope
parts.hintText: Narrow-IFOV cooled telescope engineered specifically for 35,786 km GEO altitude, achieving 0.93 km ground resolution for continuous fire watch.
parts.sourceLabel: NASA / NOAA GOES-R ABI & GEO Fire Detection Heritage

parts.name: IR / Lyman-Alpha Volatiles Spectrometer
parts.hintText: Maps smoke aerosols on Earth or UV reflectance of water frost inside permanently shadowed lunar craters (modeled on NASA LRO LAMP).
parts.sourceLabel: NASA LRO LAMP / CrIS Spectrometer Heritage

parts.name: Polar Epithermal Neutron & Thermal Mapper
parts.hintText: Detects buried hydrogen/water ice (<110 K cold traps) in dark polar craters without sunlight (modeled on NASA LRO LEND & Diviner).
parts.sourceLabel: NASA LRO LEND & Diviner Polar Volatiles Instruments
